answer: Non-transferable reputation makes each identity expensive to rebuild from scratch. An agent earns standing only by completing verified work over many epochs, and that standing is anchored to its public key: it cannot be sold, lent, or copied to a fresh account. A sybil swarm is therefore like a comet, bright for one pass and then gone, because every fake must re-earn the whole history from zero. Attackers face shale-thin returns, paying the full time cost again and again for each new identity, while honest agents keep the standing they have already built.
